title: Selected-sign expectation for a mixed triple
statement: Let $\delta\in[0,1]$, and choose a sign triple by first choosing the pair construction with probability $\delta$ and the parity construction otherwise; in the pair construction the triple is $(U,V,-V)$, and in the parity construction it is $(U,V,-UV)$, where $U,V$ are independent uniform signs. For Boolean selectors $a,b,c$, form the product of the selected signs, replacing each unselected coordinate by $1$. Its expectation is $0$ if $b\ne c$; if $b=c$, it is $-(1-\delta)$ when $a=b=c=\mathrm{true}$, $0$ when $a=\mathrm{true}$ and $b=c=\mathrm{false}$, $-\delta$ when $a=\mathrm{false}$ and $b=c=\mathrm{true}$, and $1$ when all three selectors are false.
